kold.explanation: "Kold" means "cold", for weather, drinks and food, and also for people who seem unfriendly. To say you feel cold, use "Jeg fryser" (I am freezing), not "Jeg er kold" (I am cold), which sounds as though you are an unfriendly person.

sentence.da: Det er en **kold** dag, og jeg fryser.
sentence.en: It is a cold day, and I am freezing.

kolesterol.explanation: "Kolesterol" means "cholesterol", a waxy substance in the body. Doctors check it because too much can narrow the arteries.

sentence.da: Lægen siger, at for højt **kolesterol** kan skade hjertet.
sentence.en: The doctor says that too high cholesterol can harm the heart.

kom nu.explanation: "Kom nu" means "come on", and literally "come now". It can encourage someone: "Kom nu, du kan godt!" (Come on, you can do it!). To say you do not believe something, use it with a doubtful tone: "Kom nu, det passer ikke!" (Come on, that is not true!).

forms.da: Kom nu, vi skal af sted.
forms.en: Come on, we have to go.

sentence.da: **Kom nu**, bussen kører snart!
sentence.en: Come on, the bus leaves soon!

kommende.explanation: "Kommende" means "upcoming" or "future", about something that will come: "den kommende weekend" (the coming weekend). It also fits a future role: "mine kommende kolleger" (my future colleagues).

sentence.da: Vi har et **kommende** møde på mandag.
sentence.en: We have an upcoming meeting on Monday.

kommunikation.explanation: "En kommunikation" means "communication", how people share thoughts and news with each other in speech, writing or media. It is often used for how well people understand each other at work or at home: "Vi har brug for bedre kommunikation" (We need better communication).

sentence.da: God **kommunikation** i teamet gør arbejdet lettere for alle.
sentence.en: Good communication in the team makes work easier for everyone.

kompetent.explanation: "Kompetent" means "competent", for someone who has the ability and knowledge to do a task well. It also fits the help or advice such a person gives: "kompetent hjælp" (competent help).

sentence.da: Lægen er meget **kompetent** og forklarer tingene godt.
sentence.en: The doctor is very competent and explains things well.

kompleks.explanation: "Kompleks" means "complex", something with many connected parts that is hard to understand fully. The everyday word for something hard to do is "kompliceret" (complicated).

sentence.da: Sagen er **kompleks**, fordi mange mennesker er involveret.
sentence.en: The case is complex because many people are involved.

komplet.explanation: "Komplet" means "complete", with all the parts. It can also mean "completely": "komplet umuligt" (completely impossible).

sentence.da: Vi har nu et **komplet** sæt tallerkener.
sentence.en: We now have a complete set of plates.

kompliceret.explanation: "Kompliceret" means "complicated", for a matter, rules or a situation that is hard to follow. It is the opposite of "enkel" (simple).

sentence.da: Det er en **kompliceret** situation, og ingen forstår den.
sentence.en: It is a complicated situation, and no one understands it.

kompost.explanation: "En kompost" means "compost", rotted food scraps, leaves and cuttings that turn into rich soil for plants. It is also the bin or heap where this happens: "Madaffald kommer i komposten" (Food scraps go in the compost).

sentence.da: Kartoffelskræller og blade kan blive til **kompost** i haven.
sentence.en: Potato peels and leaves can turn into compost in the garden.

koncentreret.explanation: "Koncentreret" means "focused", for a person who gives full attention to something, and "concentrated", for a liquid that is strong because there is little water in it. To say that you focus, use "at koncentrere sig" (to concentrate): "Jeg koncentrerer mig" (I am concentrating).

sentence.da: Han sidder **koncentreret** og læser hele eftermiddagen.
sentence.en: He sits focused and reads all afternoon.

kondition.explanation: "En kondition" means "fitness", how long you can run, swim or bike before you are out of breath. Do not use it for the general state of something, as English "condition" can: for that Danes say "tilstand" (condition): "bilens tilstand" (the condition of the car).

sentence.da: Jeg løber hver dag for at få bedre **kondition**.
sentence.en: I run every day to improve my fitness.

konfetti.explanation: "Konfetti" means "confetti", small colorful pieces of paper thrown to celebrate. This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Vi kaster konfetti" (We throw confetti).

sentence.da: Brudeparret fik **konfetti** over hovedet.
sentence.en: The bride and groom got confetti over their heads.

kongelig.explanation: "Kongelig" means "royal", for what belongs to the monarch or the royal family. Many Danish institutions carry it in their name, for example "Det Kongelige Teater" (The Royal Theater).

sentence.da: Hun er **kongelig** og bor på Amalienborg i København.
sentence.en: She is royal and lives at Amalienborg in Copenhagen.

konkret.explanation: "Konkret" means "concrete" in the sense of clear and specific, not general: "et konkret forslag" (a specific proposal). It is not the building material, which is called "beton" (concrete).

sentence.da: Kan du give et **konkret** eksempel, så jeg forstår det?
sentence.en: Can you give a concrete example so that I understand it?

konkurs.explanation: "Konkurs" means "bankrupt" and "bankruptcy", when a firm cannot pay what it owes and has to close. A common phrase is "at gå konkurs" (to go bankrupt): "Firmaet gik konkurs" (The company went bankrupt).

sentence.da: Butikken måtte lukke, fordi ejeren ikke kunne betale og var **konkurs**.
sentence.en: The shop had to close because the owner could not pay and was bankrupt.

konservativ.explanation: "Konservativ" means "conservative", for people or views that like traditions and prefer things to stay as they are. In Denmark it is also the name of a party, "Det Konservative Folkeparti" (The Conservative People's Party).

sentence.da: Min bedstefar er meget **konservativ** og kan ikke lide forandringer.
sentence.en: My grandfather is very conservative and does not like changes.

konstant.explanation: "Konstant" means "constant", something that keeps going without change: "Der er konstant larm" (There is constant noise). It also works for something that stays the same: "en konstant temperatur" (a constant temperature).

sentence.da: Telefonen ringer **konstant**, og det stopper aldrig.
sentence.en: The phone rings constantly, and it never stops.

kontant.explanation: "Kontant" means "cash" or "in cash". To pay by card, say "Jeg betaler med kort" (I pay by card).

sentence.da: Jeg har ikke kort og betaler **kontant**.
sentence.en: I have no card and pay in cash.

kontanthjælp.explanation: "En kontanthjælp" means "a welfare benefit", money from the municipality ("kommunen") to adults who have no work or other income. It is built from kontant (cash) and hjælp (help).

sentence.da: Hun får **kontanthjælp**, når hun hverken har job eller penge.
sentence.en: She gets welfare when she has neither a job nor money.

korrekt.explanation: "Korrekt" means "correct", and sounds a bit formal: "Svaret er korrekt" (The answer is correct). In everyday talk, people often say "rigtig" (right) instead: "Svaret er rigtigt" (The answer is right).

sentence.da: Du får point, fordi dit svar er **korrekt**.
sentence.en: You get points because your answer is correct.

korrupt.explanation: "Korrupt" means "corrupt", for people or systems that misuse power for personal gain. The matching word for the thing itself is "korruption" (corruption).

sentence.da: Dommeren tog imod penge og var derfor **korrupt**.
sentence.en: The judge accepted money and was therefore corrupt.

kort.explanation: "Kort" means "short", for length and for time. There is also a different word "et kort", which means "a card" or "a map": "et kort over byen" (a map of the city).

sentence.da: Hans hår er **kort**, ikke langt.
sentence.en: His hair is short, not long.

kort sagt.explanation: "Kort sagt" means "in short" and comes before the main point of what you have been saying. It is built from kort (short) and sagt (said).

sentence.da: **Kort sagt**, jeg kan ikke komme i morgen.
sentence.en: In short, I cannot come tomorrow.

kortvarig.explanation: "Kortvarig" means "short-lived", for an effect, a visit or a feeling that is over quickly.

sentence.da: Smerten var **kortvarig**, og efter en time var den væk.
sentence.en: The pain was short-lived, and after an hour it was gone.

kostbar.explanation: "Kostbar" means "costly" or "precious", for something worth a lot. It can be about money, but it also fits what matters to you: "kostbare minder" (precious memories).

sentence.da: Vi må ikke spilde tiden, fordi den er **kostbar**.
sentence.en: We must not waste time because it is precious.

kraftig.explanation: "Kraftig" means "strong" in the sense of powerful or heavy, such as wind, rain, blows and sounds. About a person's body it means heavily built: "en kraftig mand" (a heavily built man). For muscles and strength, Danes say "stærk" (strong) instead: "en stærk mand" (a strong man).

sentence.da: Der var **kraftig** regn hele natten, så gaden stod under vand.
sentence.en: There was heavy rain all night, so the street was flooded.

kraftigt.explanation: "Kraftigt" means "strongly" or "heavily", and tells how hard or how much something happens. In the news it often goes with change: "Valutaen faldt kraftigt" (The currency fell sharply).

sentence.da: Priserne steg **kraftigt**, og mange har svært ved at betale.
sentence.en: Prices rose sharply, and many have trouble paying.

kreativ.explanation: "Kreativ" means "creative", full of new and different ideas. You can also say it about a way of solving a problem: "en kreativ løsning" (a creative solution).

sentence.da: Hun er **kreativ** og tegner mange flotte billeder.
sentence.en: She is creative and draws many nice pictures.

kreativitet.explanation: "Kreativitet" means "creativity", the ability to think up new ideas or make something original. It is used for art, but also for solving problems at work: "Vi har brug for kreativitet i løsningen" (We need creativity in the solution).

sentence.da: Børn har masser af **kreativitet**, når de tegner og leger.
sentence.en: Children have lots of creativity when they draw and play.

kredit.explanation: "En kredit" means "credit", the right to take goods or money now and pay for them later. A shop or a bank can give it to you.

sentence.da: Hun købte sofaen på **kredit** og betaler hver måned.
sentence.en: She bought the sofa on credit and pays every month.

kriminalitet.explanation: "Kriminalitet" means "crime", all the illegal acts in a place or a time, and you use it with no "en": "Der er lidt kriminalitet her" (There is little crime here). For one act, say "en forbrydelse" (a crime): "Tyveriet var en forbrydelse" (The theft was a crime).

sentence.da: Der er meget lidt **kriminalitet** i vores lille by.
sentence.en: There is very little crime in our small town.

kriminel.explanation: "Kriminel" means "criminal", about crime or breaking the law: "kriminel adfærd" (criminal behavior). With "en" in front, "en kriminel" (a criminal) is the person who breaks the law.

sentence.da: Politiet fandt en **kriminel** bande i byen.
sentence.en: The police found a criminal gang in the city.

kristen.explanation: "Kristen" means "Christian", about the faith that follows Jesus Christ. It is written with a lowercase letter. A Christian person is "en kristen" (a Christian).

sentence.da: Hun er **kristen** og går i kirke hver søndag.
sentence.en: She is Christian and goes to church every Sunday.

kristendom.explanation: "Kristendom" means "Christianity", the religion based on the life and teaching of Jesus. This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Jeg læser om kristendom" (I am reading about Christianity).

sentence.da: **Kristendom** er den største religion i Danmark.
sentence.en: Christianity is the biggest religion in Denmark.

kritik.explanation: "Kritik" means "criticism". This word has no article, so leave out "en": "Der kom meget kritik" (There was a lot of criticism).

forms.en: He got a lot of criticism.

sentence.da: Hun fik meget **kritik** for sin tale.
sentence.en: She got a lot of criticism for her speech.

kritisk.explanation: "Kritisk" means "critical" in two ways: judging carefully and asking questions, as in "kritisk tænkning" (critical thinking), and serious or dangerous, as in "en kritisk situation" (a critical situation).

sentence.da: Man skal være **kritisk**, når man læser nyheder på nettet.
sentence.en: You should be critical when you read news online.

krudt.explanation: "Krudt" means "gunpowder", the explosive powder that was used in old guns and cannons. In the saying "Han har ikke opfundet krudtet" (He did not invent gunpowder), it means someone is not very clever.

sentence.da: Fyrværkeri indeholder **krudt**, og det brænder meget hurtigt.
sentence.en: Fireworks contain gunpowder, and it burns very fast.

krydderier.explanation: "Krydderier" means "spices", the dry things that add taste to food. Fresh green ones are "urter" (herbs).

sentence.da: Kanel og karry er **krydderier**.
sentence.en: Cinnamon and curry are spices.

krydret.explanation: "Krydret" means "spicy" or "seasoned", with lots of flavor from herbs and spices. Burning hot like chili is "stærk" (hot): "Den er for stærk" (It is too hot).

sentence.da: Karry og peber gør maden **krydret**.
sentence.en: Curry and pepper make the food spicy.

kræft.explanation: "Kræft" means "cancer", the illness where body cells grow out of control. To name the kind, put the body part in front: "hudkræft" (skin cancer).

sentence.da: Hun havde **kræft**, men blev rask efter behandlingen.
sentence.en: She had cancer but got well after the treatment.

krøllet.explanation: "Krøllet" means "curly" for hair, and "wrinkled" for cloth or paper that is not smooth.

sentence.da: Min lillesøster har **krøllet** hår, mens jeg har lige hår.
sentence.en: My little sister has curly hair, while I have straight hair.

kul.explanation: "Kul" means "coal", the black rock that is dug out of the ground and burned for heat and electricity. Charcoal for the grill is called "trækul" (charcoal).

sentence.da: Før i tiden fyrede man i ovnen med **kul** for at få varme.
sentence.en: In the past people fired the stove with coal to get warmth.

kulde.explanation: "Kulde" means "cold", the low temperature itself. Do not mix it up with "kold" (cold), which describes something: "koldt vand" (cold water).

sentence.da: Om vinteren er der sne og **kulde**.
sentence.en: In winter there is snow and cold.

kulhydrat.explanation: "Et kulhydrat" means "a carbohydrate", the part of food such as bread, pasta, rice and potatoes that gives the body energy.

sentence.da: Der er meget **kulhydrat** i pasta og ris.
sentence.en: There is a lot of carbohydrate in pasta and rice.

kulstof.explanation: "Kulstof" means "carbon", the chemical element that all living things contain. It is built from kul (coal) and stof (substance), so literally "coal stuff".

sentence.da: Planter og dyr består blandt andet af **kulstof**.
sentence.en: Plants and animals consist partly of carbon.

kun.explanation: "Kun" means "only" or "just", and it limits the word that comes after it. "Kun jeg ved det" means "Only I know it", while "Jeg ved kun det" means "That is all I know".

sentence.da: Jeg har **kun** to kroner.
sentence.en: I only have two kroner.

kundeservice.explanation: "Kundeservice" means "customer service", the part of a company that helps customers. It is built from en kunde (a customer) and service.

sentence.da: Jeg ringede til **kundeservice**, men ingen svarede.
sentence.en: I called customer service, but nobody answered.

kundskab.explanation: "En kundskab" means "knowledge", what you have learned about a subject. The plural "kundskaber" is common for what someone knows in school or work: "gode kundskaber i matematik" (good knowledge of math).

sentence.da: Lægen har stor **kundskab** om kroppen og sygdomme.
sentence.en: The doctor has great knowledge about the body and diseases.

kunst.explanation: "Kunst" means "art", the things people make to look at. A work of art is "et kunstværk", and a person who makes art is "en kunstner" (an artist).

sentence.da: Hun elsker **kunst** og maler hver weekend.
sentence.en: She loves art and paints every weekend.

kunstig intelligens.explanation: "Kunstig intelligens" means "artificial intelligence", software that can write, translate or recognize pictures. It is built from kunstig (artificial) and intelligens (intelligence), and people often say AI for short.

sentence.da: Mange bruger **kunstig intelligens** til at skrive tekster.
sentence.en: Many people use artificial intelligence to write texts.

kvalificeret.explanation: "Kvalificeret" means "qualified", for someone with the education or experience a job needs. It is also used for a guess or an opinion that rests on real knowledge: "et kvalificeret gæt" (an informed guess).

sentence.da: Hun er **kvalificeret** til jobbet, fordi hun har studeret i fem år.
sentence.en: She is qualified for the job because she has studied for five years.

kvalm.explanation: "Kvalm" means "nauseous", how you feel when your stomach is upset and you might vomit. For being sick, use "syg" (sick): "Jeg er syg" (I am sick).

sentence.da: Jeg er **kvalm**, og jeg har ondt i maven.
sentence.en: I am nauseous and my stomach hurts.

kvalme.explanation: "En kvalme" means "nausea", the sick feeling you get before you throw up. It is also used about things you find disgusting: "Det giver mig kvalme" (It makes me sick).

sentence.da: Efter turen på båden fik jeg **kvalme** og måtte sidde ned.
sentence.en: After the boat trip I felt nauseous and had to sit down.

kvart.explanation: "Kvart" means "quarter" and is used when telling the time. "Kvart over tre" (a quarter past three) is 3:15, and "kvart i fire" (a quarter to four) is 3:45. A quarter of an hour is "et kvarter" (15 minutes).

sentence.da: Vi ses **kvart** over tre.
sentence.en: See you at a quarter past three.

kvart i.explanation: "Kvart i" means "quarter to". "Kvart i tre" is 2:45, fifteen minutes before three. Do not mix it up with "kvart over" (quarter past): "kvart over tre" is 3:15.

sentence.da: Filmen starter **kvart i** syv.
sentence.en: The movie starts at a quarter to seven.

kvart over.explanation: "Kvart over" means "quarter past", so "kvart over tre" is 3:15. Here "over" means "past". Do not mix it up with "kvart i" (quarter to): "kvart i tre" is 2:45.

sentence.da: Bussen kommer **kvart over** otte.
sentence.en: The bus comes at a quarter past eight.

kvik.explanation: "Kvik" means "quick", but about thinking and speaking, not about running: a person who understands fast and answers well. For speed in movement, Danes use "hurtig" (fast): "en hurtig bil" (a fast car).

sentence.da: Hun er **kvik** og forstår det med det samme.
sentence.en: She is quick and understands it right away.

kvindelig.explanation: "Kvindelig" means "female", and also "feminine", as in a feminine quality. It is built from kvinde (woman).

sentence.da: Min læge er **kvindelig**, ikke mandlig.
sentence.en: My doctor is female, not male.

kvit.explanation: "Kvit" means "even" or "quits", when nobody owes the other person anything, for example after paying back money or returning a favor. In the phrase "blive kvit med" (get rid of), it means getting rid of something: "Jeg vil blive kvit med min forkølelse" (I want to get rid of my cold).

sentence.da: Nu har jeg betalt min gæld, og vi er **kvit**.
sentence.en: Now I have paid my debt and we are even.

kvæg.explanation: "Kvæg" means "cattle", the farm animals kept for milk and meat. This word has no article, so leave out "et": "Vi har kvæg på gården" (We have cattle on the farm). For one animal, say "en ko" (a cow) or "en tyr" (a bull).

sentence.da: Landmanden har hundrede stykker **kvæg** på marken.
sentence.en: The farmer has a hundred head of cattle in the field.

kylling.explanation: "Kylling" means "chicken", both the bird and the meat you eat. For the meat, you say just "kylling" with no "en" in front, as in "kylling med ris" (chicken with rice).

sentence.da: Vi spiser **kylling** til aftensmad.
sentence.en: We are eating chicken for dinner.

kål.explanation: "Kål" means "cabbage", a round vegetable that is eaten raw or cooked. It is part of many words, such as "hvidkål" (white cabbage) and "rødkål" (red cabbage).

sentence.da: **Kål** er en grøn grøntsag med mange blade.
sentence.en: Cabbage is a green vegetable with many leaves.

kær.explanation: "Kær" means "dear", for someone you love or care about. Letters start with it: "Kære Anna" (Dear Anna), and "Kære alle" means "Dear everyone".

sentence.da: Han er en **kær** ven, og jeg savner ham.
sentence.en: He is a dear friend, and I miss him.

kærlig.explanation: "Kærlig" means "loving" or "affectionate", warm and caring toward others. At the end of a letter, "Kærlig hilsen" means "With love".

sentence.da: Min bedstemor er altid så **kærlig** mod os.
sentence.en: My grandmother is always so loving toward us.

kærlighed.explanation: "Kærlighed" means "love", the main word for the feeling. To say "I love you", Danes use "at elske" (to love) instead: "Jeg elsker dig" (I love you).

sentence.da: Mor viser sin **kærlighed** med et kram.
sentence.en: Mom shows her love with a hug.

kærnemælk.explanation: "Kærnemælk" means "buttermilk", a sour, slightly thick milk drink. It is built from kærne (churn) and mælk (milk), because it was traditionally the liquid left when cream is churned into butter.

sentence.da: **Kærnemælk** smager surt, men jeg kan godt lide den.
sentence.en: Buttermilk tastes sour, but I like it.

kød.explanation: "Kød" means "meat" of any kind, and you use it with no "et": "Jeg spiser kød" (I eat meat). To name the kind of meat, put a word in front, as in "oksekød" (beef) or "svinekød" (pork).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gerne **kød** og fisk.
sentence.en: I like eating meat and fish.

kølig.explanation: "Kølig" means "cool", slightly cold but not unpleasant. For truly cold, use "kold" (cold): "Vandet er koldt" (The water is cold).

sentence.da: Jeg tog en jakke på, fordi aftenen var **kølig**.
sentence.en: I put on a jacket because the evening was cool.

køn.explanation: "Køn" means "pretty", usually about a person, a face or a place. Do not mix it up with "et køn", a different word that means "gender" (male or female).

sentence.da: Hun er en **køn** pige med langt hår.
sentence.en: She is a pretty girl with long hair.

at lade.explanation: "At lade" means "to let", to allow someone to do something. It can also mean "to leave something as it is": "Jeg lader nøglen ligge" (I leave the key lying there).

sentence.da: Mor vil ikke **lade** os gå alene.
sentence.en: Mom won't let us go alone.

at lade som om.explanation: "At lade som om" means "to pretend". To state what you pretend, add a full sentence after "som om" (as if): "Han lader som om han sover" (He pretends he is sleeping).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **lade som om** de er pirater.
sentence.en: The children want to pretend they are pirates.

at lade være.explanation: "At lade være" means "to refrain from" doing something. To name the activity you refrain from, add "med at" (with to) and a verb: "Jeg lader være med at ryge" (I refrain from smoking). As a short command, "Lad være!" means "Don't!".

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lade være** med at spise slik.
sentence.en: I will refrain from eating candy.

at lande.explanation: "At lande" means "to land", when a plane or a bird comes down and touches the ground.

sentence.da: Flyet skal **lande** om en time.
sentence.en: The plane will land in an hour.

at lappe.explanation: "At lappe" means "to patch / mend", to fix a hole by putting a piece of cloth or rubber over it, as on a bike tire or a pair of trousers.

sentence.da: Jeg skal **lappe** hullet i cykelslangen i aften.
sentence.en: I have to patch the hole in the bike tube tonight.

at larme.explanation: "At larme" means "to make noise": "Børnene larmer" (The children are making noise).

sentence.da: Børnene må ikke **larme** efter klokken ti.
sentence.en: The children must not make noise after ten o'clock.

at lave.explanation: "At lave" means "to make" or "to do". It is used for creating something, such as "Jeg laver en kage" (I am making a cake), and for what you are busy with: "Hvad laver du?" (What are you doing?).

forms.en: I have made / I have done

sentence.da: Hvad skal vi **lave** i aften?
sentence.en: What are we going to do tonight?

at lave en fejl.explanation: "At lave en fejl" means "to make a mistake". For more than one mistake, drop "en": "Alle laver fejl" (Everyone makes mistakes).

sentence.da: Jeg er bange for at **lave en fejl**.
sentence.en: I am afraid of making a mistake.

at lave lektier.explanation: "At lave lektier" means "to do homework". Danish says "lave" (to make) where English says "do": "Har du lavet dine lektier?" (Have you done your homework?).

sentence.da: Børnene skal **lave lektier** nu.
sentence.en: The children have to do homework now.

at lave mad.explanation: "At lave mad" means "to cook". It is built from lave (to make) and mad (food), so literally it is "to make food". To name the dish, drop "mad": "Jeg laver pasta" (I am making pasta).

sentence.da: Min far vil **lave mad** i aften.
sentence.en: My father will cook tonight.

at lave om.explanation: "At lave om" means "to change" or "to redo" something you already made. To change only part of something, add "på" (on): "Jeg laver om på planen" (I am changing the plan).

sentence.da: Hun skal **lave om** på hele rapporten.
sentence.en: She has to change the whole report.

at lave sjov.explanation: "At lave sjov" means "to joke around". To tease someone, add "med" (with): "Hun laver sjov med mig" (She is teasing me).

sentence.da: Min bror elsker at **lave sjov**, og alle griner.
sentence.en: My brother loves to joke around, and everyone laughs.

at le.explanation: "At le" means "to laugh". To laugh at someone, add "af" (at): "Han ler af mig" (He is laughing at me).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **le** af den sjove film.
sentence.en: The children want to laugh at the funny movie.

at lede.explanation: "At lede" means "to lead": "Hun leder holdet" (She leads the team). With "efter" (for) it means "to search": "Jeg leder efter mine nøgler" (I'm looking for my keys).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **lede** efter min hat.
sentence.en: I have to look for my hat.

at lede efter.explanation: "At lede efter" means "to look for" something you cannot find yet. For something you can already see, use "at se på" (to look at): "Jeg ser på billedet" (I am looking at the picture).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lede efter** mine nøgler.
sentence.en: I want to look for my keys.

at legalisere.explanation: "At legalisere" means "to legalize", to make something allowed that was not allowed before. For a document, it means to have it confirmed as official: "at legalisere et dokument" (to have a document certified).

sentence.da: Nogle lande vil **legalisere** cannabis til medicinsk brug.
sentence.en: Some countries want to legalize cannabis for medical use.

at lege.explanation: "At lege" means "to play" the way children do, just for fun. For sports, games and instruments, Danish uses "at spille" (to play).

sentence.da: Børnene vil **lege** med bolden i haven.
sentence.en: The children want to play with the ball in the garden.

at legitimere.explanation: "At legitimere" means "to legitimize", to make something accepted as right. With "sig" (oneself) it means "to show ID": "Du skal legitimere dig i banken" (You must show ID at the bank).

sentence.da: Du skal **legitimere** dig med pas eller kørekort.
sentence.en: You must show ID with a passport or driver's license.

at leje.explanation: "At leje" means "to rent", when you pay to use something. For the owner who rents it out, use "at udleje" (to rent out).

sentence.da: Vi vil **leje** en bil i weekenden.
sentence.en: We want to rent a car for the weekend.

at lempe.explanation: "At lempe" means "to ease" or "to relax" a rule or a requirement so it becomes less strict: "lempe kravene" (ease the requirements). For pain, use "at lindre" (to relieve).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **lempe** reglerne for rejser til udlandet.
sentence.en: The government will relax the rules for travel abroad.

at lette.explanation: "At lette" means "to take off", for a plane. With a task, it means "to make easier": "Det letter arbejdet" (That makes the work easier).

sentence.da: Flyet skal **lette** om fem minutter.
sentence.en: The plane takes off in five minutes.

at leve.explanation: "At leve" means "to live (be alive)": "Hun lever stadig" (She is still alive). It also means how you live your life: "leve et godt liv" (to live a good life). For where your home is, use "at bo" (to live somewhere).

sentence.da: Fisk kan ikke **leve** uden vand.
sentence.en: Fish cannot live without water.

at lide.explanation: "At lide" means "to suffer", usually with "af" (from): "Han lider af hovedpine" (He suffers from headaches). Do not mix it up with "kan lide" (like): "Jeg kan lide kaffe" (I like coffee).

sentence.da: Dyrene vil **lide**, når der ikke er mere vand.
sentence.en: The animals will suffer when there is no more water.

at ligge.explanation: "At ligge" means "to lie (be lying)", to be lying down or placed flat: "Bogen ligger på bordet" (The book is lying on the table). It is also used for where places are located: "Byen ligger ved havet" (The town is by the sea). Do not mix it up with "at lægge" (to put something down).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ligge** i sengen og sove.
sentence.en: I want to lie in bed and sleep.

at ligge syg.explanation: "At ligge syg" means "to be ill in bed", too sick to get up. To say simply that you are sick, use "at være syg" (to be sick).

forms.en: I have been ill in bed

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **ligge syg** hele ugen.
sentence.en: I cannot lie in bed sick all week.

at ligne.explanation: "At ligne" means "to look like", and it always compares two things: "Drengen ligner sin far" (The boy looks like his father). To describe how someone looks, use "at se ud" (to look): "Du ser træt ud" (You look tired).

sentence.da: Hun kan **ligne** sin mor, når hun smiler.
sentence.en: She can look like her mother when she smiles.

at like.explanation: "At like" means "to like (online)": "Hun liker alle mine opslag" (She likes all my posts). For liking something outside the internet, such as a person or food, use "at kunne lide" (to like).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **like** dit billede på Instagram.
sentence.en: I want to like your picture on Instagram.

at lindre.explanation: "At lindre" means "to relieve" pain or suffering, so that it hurts less, though it may not go away completely: "Tabletten lindrer hovedpinen" (The pill relieves the headache).

sentence.da: Varme kan **lindre** smerten i ryggen.
sentence.en: Heat can relieve the pain in the back.

at logge ind.explanation: "At logge ind" means "to log in", to get into an app or website by showing who you are. The opposite is "at logge ud" (to log out).

sentence.da: Du skal **logge ind** for at se dine beskeder.
sentence.en: You have to log in to see your messages.

at logge ud.explanation: "At logge ud" means "to log out", to leave an app or website when you are finished so that nobody else can use it.

sentence.da: Du skal **logge ud** på en fælles computer.
sentence.en: You should log out on a shared computer.
